_meta.purpose: Fund-lifecycle events on a timeline, anchored to the district ledger, grouped into story chains. The atomic unit of the news/timeline layer. See news-timeline-schema.md.
_meta.rules: Same sourcing discipline as the ledger: every event carries a source + tier and a confidence (documented = gov source / reported = news only / alleged). amount_cr stays null unless PDF-cited (figure_gap). No event is fabricated; seeds are real, ledger-anchored stories.
_meta.coverage: 2 seed story chains (Birbhum MGNREGS freeze; Kolkata KMC grant dependency). Built to be extended by ingest_news.py + human anchoring.
_meta.scheme_ref_note: scheme_ref resolves against district-ledger.json _meta.scheme_registry / scheme_aliases. official_ref resolves against the district roster role keys + _meta.authority_map.
_meta.accountability_chain: Each story_chain can carry the full accountability arc: promise -> result -> actual_cost -> human_impact. This is the 'source vs bias vs stated promise vs result vs actual (per-capita) cost' unit. Rules that keep it defensible:

accountability_rules.promise: The political entity's OWN stated commitment ONLY (manifesto / budget speech / scheme launch / official release), QUOTED with a source URL. We never infer motive or 'agenda' — we quote what was promised and cite it. entity = the body that made the promise (govt/ministry/party as stated in the source), never an accusation.
accountability_rules.result: What is documented to have happened, sourced. Factual (delivered / delayed / withheld / lapsed), never a verdict.
accountability_rules.actual_cost: Total amount_cr AND per_capita_inr, EACH cited. per_capita = amount / Census-2011 population at the stated scope (district or state). scope MUST be labelled — never pass a state figure off as per-district. figure_gap=true until the amount is sourced.
accountability_rules.human_impact: Plain-language, factual statement of what this meant for residents (what was denied or delivered) — 'human value, not economic contribution'. No adjectives of blame; state the concrete effect.
accountability_rules.social_line: A ready-to-post one-liner (<=200 chars) for auto social posting (share.html / post_to_social.py). Facts + figure + source-implied, never an accusation.

_meta.per_capita_note: per_capita_inr is rupees per resident (amount_cr * 1e7 / population). Population from district-pop.json (Census 2011). Scope 'state' uses the summed state population; 'district' uses the district population. Shown to make cost HUMAN and comparable, not to assert contribution.

story_chains.title: Birbhum's MGNREGS money: frozen at the top for four years
story_chains.one_line: Centre froze WB's MGNREGS funds under Sec 27 (Mar 2022); ₹3,038 cr dues piled up; resumed Jun 2026 after Supreme Court intervention. Dysfunction = money WITHHELD upstream, not misspent.

promise.stated: MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adults volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

result.stated: Fund release to West Bengal was frozen from 9 Mar 2022 under Sec 27; no MGNREGS wages flowed to WB districts for ~4 years until a June 2026 resumption after Supreme Court intervention.

actual_cost.amount_note: Centre-stated pending MGNREGS dues to WB (Rajya Sabha, 2025) — the withheld amount, not district-split.
actual_cost.per_capita_note: ₹3,038 cr ÷ WB Census-2011 population — ₹333 of guaranteed-wage money withheld per WB resident (state scope; NOT Birbhum-specific).

source.title: Centre owes ₹3,000 crore MGNREGA dues to Bengal (Rajya Sabha)

story_chains.human_impact: The statutory job guarantee stopped functioning in WB's rural districts: households that would have earned MGNREGS wages did not, unbuilt assets and reported distress migration followed. ~₹333 of guaranteed-wage money per resident sat withheld upstream.
story_chains.social_line: West Bengal's MGNREGS job-guarantee funds were frozen by the Centre for ~4 years — ₹3,038 cr in dues, ~₹333 per resident withheld — until the Supreme Court pushed a June 2026 restart. [sourced]

story_chains.title: Kolkata's civic money: over half flows down as grant
story_chains.one_line: KMC's BE 2025-26 shows ₹2,897 cr of ₹5,525 cr receipts are Central+State grant — 52% grant-dependent, budget in deficit.

promise.stated: KMC's Budget Estimate 2025-26 projects total receipts of ₹5,524.84 cr to fund the city's civic services for the year.

result.stated: Of ₹5,524.84 cr total receipts, ₹2,897 cr (~52%) is Central + State Grant-in-Aid rather than locally raised revenue; the budget is in deficit.

actual_cost.amount_note: Central + State grant component of KMC's BE 2025-26 receipts (the money that flows DOWN rather than being raised locally).
actual_cost.per_capita_note: ₹2,897 cr ÷ Kolkata Census-2011 population — ₹6,443 of the city's per-resident civic money comes from grant, not local revenue.

story_chains.human_impact: For every Kolkata resident, about ₹6,443 of the year's civic spending depends on grant money flowing down from the Centre and State — so local services are exposed to how reliably that upstream money arrives.
story_chains.social_line: 52% of Kolkata's ₹5,525 cr civic budget is grant, not locally raised — ~₹6,443 per resident depends on money flowing down from above. [KMC BE 2025-26, gov PDF]

story_chains.title: West Bengal's DA arrears: 11 years of delayed pay, settled by the Supreme Court
story_chains.one_line: State employees' dearness allowance fell years behind central rates; after a 2022 Calcutta HC order the Supreme Court finally ruled (5 Feb 2026) that WB must clear ~11 years of DA arrears (2009–2019, ~₹10,000 cr under the 5th Pay Commission) to ~20 lakh employees.

promise.stated: Dearness Allowance is a legally enforceable component of a government employee's pay, payable to compensate for inflation.

source.title: Supreme Court orders West Bengal to pay 11 years of DA arrears to employees

result.stated: DA disbursal lagged central rates for years; the Supreme Court's 5 Feb 2026 judgment upheld the employees' entitlement and directed WB to clear arrears for 2009–2019, with a court-monitored committee (chaired by Justice Indu Malhotra) fixing the instalment schedule.

actual_cost.amount_note: Approx. DA arrears for 2009–2019 under the 5th Pay Commission, as reported around the Supreme Court proceedings. A court-appointed committee is fixing the exact figure and schedule.
actual_cost.per_capita_note: ≈₹10,000 cr ÷ ~20 lakh WB state employees ≈ ₹50,000 of delayed pay per employee (order of magnitude; the committee is fixing exact per-employee dues). Population here is the ~20 lakh AFFECTED EMPLOYEES, not state residents — labelled as such.

source.title: DA outstanding of ₹10,000 crore to be cleared under 5th Pay Commission: SC orders

story_chains.human_impact: About 20 lakh West Bengal government employees went years without DA at central rates — on the order of ₹50,000 of delayed pay each — until the Supreme Court's Feb 2026 judgment made the arrears legally due and set up a monitored payout.
story_chains.social_line: The Supreme Court has ordered West Bengal to clear ~11 years of DA arrears — about ₹10,000 cr, ~₹50,000 of delayed pay per employee — for ~20 lakh state employees. [SC judgment, Feb 2026]

story_chains.title: Punjab's pension arrears: age-staggered payout struck down, full release ordered
story_chains.one_line: Punjab tried to pay pension arrears in age-based instalments; the Punjab & Haryana High Court quashed that plan as arbitrary (Article 14) and ordered pending DA/DR released to ~4 lakh pensioners (and ~3.5 lakh employees) at central rates by 30 Jun 2026 — implementation reportedly still pending.

promise.stated: Punjab accepted payment of DA/DR to its pensioners and employees on the Central Government pattern (per the 6th Punjab Pay Commission).

source.title: Punjab & Haryana High Court quashes staggered pension arrears plan, directs Punjab to release pending DA/DR

result.stated: Punjab delayed the DA/DR citing financial constraints and issued a Feb 2025 plan staggering arrears by age. The High Court struck that down as arbitrary and violative of Article 14, and directed release to all employees & pensioners at the All-India-Service rate by 30 Jun 2026, with the Chief Secretary to report compliance. Reports say implementation remained pending.

actual_cost.amount_note: No single clean sourced rupee total for the Punjab pension arrears — left an explicit gap. The DOCUMENTED scale is the headcount: ~4 lakh pensioners (and ~3.5 lakh employees), ~7.5 lakh people awaiting their legal dues.
actual_cost.affected_note: ~7.5 lakh serving employees + pensioners across Punjab (of which ~4 lakh pensioners), per reporting on the case.

source.title: Punjab pending DA dispute: 7.5 lakh employees and pensioners waiting for their legal due

story_chains.human_impact: About 4 lakh Punjab pensioners (with ~3.5 lakh serving employees, ~7.5 lakh in all) were kept waiting for DA/DR they were legally owed — while All-India-Service officers drew full benefits from the same Consolidated Fund, a disparity the High Court flagged. The exact rupee arrears per pensioner is a gap; the documented fact is the delay and its scale.
story_chains.social_line: A court struck down Punjab's plan to pay pension arrears in age-based instalments as arbitrary — ~4 lakh pensioners (7.5 lakh in all) are owed DA/DR at central rates, ordered released by 30 Jun 2026. [P&H High Court]

fiscal_events.title: Centre freezes MGNREGS fund release to West Bengal (Sec 27)
fiscal_events.summary: The Union stopped MGNREGS fund release to West Bengal from 9 March 2022 under Section 27 of the MGNREGA Act, citing non-compliance/corruption. Every MGNREGS-dependent district, including Birbhum, was cut off from wages at source.

primary_source.title: MGNREGS in West Bengal — why it was halted

fiscal_events.title: Pending MGNREGS dues to WB reach ₹3,038 cr (highest of any state)
fiscal_events.summary: Per the Centre's figure in the Rajya Sabha (2025), pending MGNREGS dues to West Bengal stood at ₹3,038 cr — the highest of any state. The state claims ₹18,000 cr across MGNREGS + PMAY-G. Rural districts like Birbhum bore the brunt: assets unbuilt, migration.

primary_source.title: Centre owes ₹3,000 crore MGNREGA dues to Bengal (Rajya Sabha)

fiscal_events.amount_note: ₹3,038 cr is a Centre-stated Rajya Sabha figure (news-reported); upgrade to the Lok Sabha/RS Q&A PDF for tier-1.

fiscal_events.summary: After roughly four years of frozen funds, Supreme Court intervention paved the way for MGNREGS to restart in West Bengal.

fiscal_events.title: MGNREGS work resumes in West Bengal
fiscal_events.summary: MGNREGS work resumed in West Bengal on 1 June 2026 after the near-four-year freeze, restoring the rural job-guarantee channel to districts like Birbhum.

fiscal_events.title: KMC budget: ₹2,897 cr of ₹5,525 cr receipts are Central+State grant
fiscal_events.summary: Kolkata Municipal Corporation's Budget Estimate 2025-26 records a 'Government Grant' (Central + State Grant-in-Aid) of ₹2,897 cr against total receipts of ₹5,524.84 cr — about 52% of the city's civic money flows down as grant, not raised locally. The budget is in deficit.

severity.basis: ₹2897 cr → money 4/4; state → people 4/4; stage 'release' → governance 0/4

fiscal_events.title: Calcutta High Court orders WB to pay DA at central rates
fiscal_events.summary: The Calcutta High Court ruled that West Bengal must align its dearness-allowance disbursal with central government rates, treating DA as an enforceable entitlement of state employees. The state challenged the order in the Supreme Court.

primary_source.title: Supreme Court orders West Bengal to pay 11 years of DA arrears to employees

fiscal_events.title: Supreme Court interim order: WB to pay 25% of DA arrears in 6 weeks
fiscal_events.summary: The Supreme Court directed West Bengal to pay 25% of the outstanding DA arrears (accumulated 2009–2019 under the 5th Pay Commission, ~₹10,000 cr) to its employees within six weeks — an interim step while the balance was worked out.
fiscal_events.amount_note: ≈₹10,000 cr total 2009–2019 DA arrears (the 25% interim is a portion); figure as reported around the proceedings.

primary_source.title: DA outstanding of ₹10,000 crore to be cleared under 5th Pay Commission: SC orders

fiscal_events.title: Supreme Court final judgment: WB must clear ~11 years of DA arrears
fiscal_events.summary: On 5 Feb 2026 the Supreme Court upheld employees' entitlement and directed West Bengal to clear DA arrears for 2009–2019 for ~20 lakh employees, with a court-appointed committee (chaired by former Justice Indu Malhotra, with the CAG or a nominee) fixing the exact amount and instalment schedule. Amounts paid are not to be recovered even if the law later changes.

primary_source.title: SC orders West Bengal to release DA arrears to employees (verdict)

fiscal_events.title: Punjab issues a plan to pay pension arrears in age-based instalments
fiscal_events.summary: Citing financial constraints, Punjab issued a 'Liquidation Plan' dated 18 Feb 2025 that staggered payment of pension DA/DR arrears based on the pensioner's age — deferring dues the state had accepted on the Central Government pattern.

primary_source.title: Punjab & Haryana High Court quashes staggered pension arrears plan

fiscal_events.title: High Court quashes the age-staggered plan, orders full release
fiscal_events.summary: The Punjab & Haryana High Court struck down the age-based staggering as arbitrary and violative of Article 14, directing the state and its corporations to release all pending DA/DR to employees and pensioners at the All-India-Service (central) rate by 30 Jun 2026, with the Chief Secretary to file a compliance report.

primary_source.title: Punjab & Haryana High Court directs Punjab to release pending DA/DR

fiscal_events.title: Deadline arrives; implementation reportedly still pending
fiscal_events.summary: As of the court-set 30 Jun 2026 deadline, reporting indicated Punjab had yet to implement the revised DA/DR for its ~3.5 lakh employees and ~4 lakh pensioners, again citing fiscal constraints — leaving ~7.5 lakh people awaiting their legally-affirmed dues.

primary_source.title: Punjab pending DA dispute: 7.5 lakh employees and pensioners waiting for their legal due
